description: Search the Nevermined Agent Services Catalog for paid services, ranked by ARD HYBRID relevance — semantic (meaning) matches merged with lexical (keyword) matches, most relevant first — falling back to pure lexical when the embedding provider is unavailable. Each result includes a closed matchReason, a per-item rankingSource, and one scale-specific score. A query is required; the other filters are optional. Each listing is concise: `slug` (what get_service, quote_service and pay_service take), `displayName`, a one-line `description`, `tags`, `protocol`, `network`, prices (`priceLabel`, the listing's advertised price; `headlinePriceLabel`, derived from endpoint prices, where "from" means prices vary; and `displayPriceLabel`, which covers the whole listing: what calls to it, on any endpoint, settled at when `displayPriceSource` is `settled`, the merchant's latest quote when `quoted`), `freeAfterPurchasePaths` (path prefixes free to poll after your own paid call, within the follow-up window; a 402 under one is still paid; see get_service), health and payability (`healthStatus`, `uptime30d`, `successRate`, `verificationStatus`, `routerPayable`), and `endpoints`, each with its `method`, `path`, `invokePath` (on an untemplated path, the subpath to send, where `""` means the service base already is the endpoint; a templated path, one with a `:name`, `{name}`, `<name>` or `*` segment, URL-encoded or not, has none: call get_service and send its `payServiceArgs.path` with each `pathParams` segment, whether a placeholder or the example's value, replaced by your own), `priceLabel` and `description` (plus `access` or `auth` when set). A field is omitted when it is unknown or withheld, never defaulted: a missing `healthStatus` does not mean healthy. A `rankingSource: "federated"` hit comes from another registry: it has no slug and cannot be quoted or paid here. Budget against the selected endpoint price and quote before paying. Request shapes and examples are not in a search result: call get_service on the slug before paying. `detail: true` returns every listing in full as the catalog publishes it: about 6 KB per listing on average, far more for a listing with many endpoints. A concise listing is roughly 1–2 KB, so a large page is still large. Only the first page is returned and the `pageToken` in the result cannot be passed back to this tool: to see other matches, narrow the query or filters first, and raise `pageSize` (up to 100) only when that is not enough. Discovery only; no payment. To have the platform PICK (and optionally pay) the single best service for a need instead of choosing yourself, use route_by_intent.

category.description: Restrict to services carrying this catalog tag — it filters on tags exactly like `tag`. The category names `list_categories` returns are not stored as tags, so passing one here matches nothing; put a category name in `query` instead. Given together, `category` and `tag` match a service carrying either one.

detail.description: Return every listing in full, with each endpoint’s request and response shapes, examples and quote. Large; to read one listing, prefer get_service.

exclude.description: Never return this opaque catalog slug in the result page.

funding.description: Only services with at least one endpoint payable with Nevermined credits. Local catalog only. Check get_service: the specific endpoint carries subscription when credits can pay it; this does not check your balance.

pageSize.description: Page size, 1–100 (a size of 0 is meaningless and is rejected).

prefer.description: Move this opaque catalog slug to the front when it matched the returned page; if it did not match, keep the normal ranked fallback.

protocol.description: Restrict to a payment protocol. Only x402 and mpp are payable via the Router.

query.description: What you need, in plain language. REQUIRED. Ranked semantically AND lexically (hybrid), most relevant first — a query describing the need ("translate documents to German") matches on meaning, not only exact words, and also keyword-matches title, descriptions and tags. Falls back to keyword-only ranking when the embedding provider is unavailable.

tag.description: Restrict to services carrying this catalog tag (e.g. a protocol or domain keyword from a listing's `tags`). Combined with `category` it widens the match to either value rather than narrowing it.
